# Requirements Quality Checklist: Claude Code guidance and pipeline gating

**Purpose**: Validate that the requirements in `spec.md` are complete, unambiguous, mutually consistent and objectively verifiable, before planning turns them into design decisions

**Created**: 2026-09-05

**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.

**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## MUST-to-requirement traceability

- [ ] CHK001 Does every `MUST` stated in the originating task map to exactly one functional requirement, with no `MUST` silently dropped and none split across two requirements that could drift? [Traceability, Spec §Input]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the task's "limit 10" for parallel readers represented by exactly one requirement rather than by a requirement and a separate success criterion that could disagree? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018, §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the task's three branch-mode and four worktree-mode workspace choices each individually enumerated in the requirements, rather than summarized as "the appropriate choices"? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022, §FR-023]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the requirement set distinguish the task's `MUST` items from its `MAY` items, so that FR-018 and FR-024 are not read as obligations? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018, §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK005 Is a requirement-ID scheme established and used consistently across functional requirements, success criteria and acceptance scenarios? [Traceability]

## Requirements asserting an existing property

- [ ] CHK006 Does FR-007 state how the under-200-line property is to be proven, rather than asserting that it holds? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK007 Does FR-007 state how "reaches its detailed rules on demand" is to be proven, given that on-demand loading is a behaviour rather than a countable property? [Measurability, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the prohibition on manufacturing a change in order to appear to satisfy FR-007 stated as a requirement, or only as narrative? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-007a]
- [ ] CHK009 Does FR-007a define "what belongs in such a file" by reference to something a reviewer can check, rather than leaving it to judgement? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007a]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the boundary between FR-007a's prohibition on reordering and FR-028's obligation to correct untrue statements explicit enough that an editor knows which edits to that file are permitted? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007a, §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK011 Does SC-003 specify who performs the measurement and against which file, so the criterion is verifiable without ambiguity about which instruction file is meant? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]

## Correction and supersession obligations

- [ ] CHK012 Does FR-028 identify the statements to be corrected, or does it only assert that such statements will be found? [Completeness, Spec §FR-028]
- [ ] CHK013 Is there a requirement that the set of statements rendered untrue be enumerated before implementation begins, so that "every statement" is a checkable set rather than an open-ended one? [Measurability, Spec §FR-028, Gap]
- [ ] CHK014 Does FR-029 define which kinds of record must be superseded rather than edited, distinguishing a committed contract from ordinary documentation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-029]
- [ ] CHK015 Are the criteria for deciding "corrected in place" versus "superseded by a new record" stated, given that FR-028 and FR-029 prescribe opposite treatments? [Consistency, Spec §FR-028, §FR-029]
- [ ] CHK016 Does SC-011 express a verifiable end state for the corrections, rather than requiring a reviewer to prove a negative across the whole repository? [Measurability, Spec §SC-011]
- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements defined for what happens if a statement rendered untrue is discovered after implementation has begun? [Coverage, Gap]

## Requirement completeness

- [ ] CHK018 Are requirements defined for what a phase proposal must contain when a phase is conditional and about to be skipped, rather than invoked? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the behaviour specified for a phase proposal that is revised more than a bounded number of times? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK020 Are requirements defined for what the boundary check does when the working tree cannot be inspected at all — no repository, or an inaccessible one? [Edge Case, Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK021 Does the spec define what happens when the conflict-resolution workflow is reached but does not resolve the conflict? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK022 Are requirements defined for the case where no review request is ever created, so the workspace question's trigger never fires? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-021]
- [ ] CHK023 Are requirements defined for what a parallel reader must do when it finds nothing, so that an empty result is distinguishable from a reader that searched the wrong place? [Completeness, Gap, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK024 Is the relationship between FR-009's gating obligation and the specific decisions it governs stated concretely enough to check, rather than as "every decision that changes the repository"? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]

## Requirement clarity

- [ ] CHK025 Is "the exact argument" in FR-010 defined precisely enough that a proposal showing a summarized or truncated argument would fail the requirement? [Clarity, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK026 Is "what changed since the drafted plan" in FR-013 defined, including whether "nothing changed" must be stated explicitly? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK027 Is "an interrupted integration" in FR-014 defined by enumeration, or left to interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK028 Is "durably enough that a run which has been summarized can still report it" in FR-017 expressed as a checkable property rather than as a rationale? [Measurability, Spec §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK029 Is "genuinely independent read-only questions" in FR-018 defined well enough that a reviewer could reject a batch that does not meet it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK030 Is "the choice that discards least" in FR-025 unambiguous when two choices discard different things — a branch versus a working directory? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK031 Is "anything in the workspace is uncommitted or unpushed" in FR-026 scoped to the run's own output, or to the whole tree including pre-existing edits? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK032 Is "any blanket approval given earlier in the run" in FR-027 defined, given that the spec does not elsewhere establish that such approvals exist? [Clarity, Assumption, Spec §FR-027]

## Requirement consistency

- [ ] CHK033 Do FR-008's reachability requirement and FR-009's gating requirement together state the safety argument, or does FR-008 stand alone in a way that permits reachability without the gates? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK034 Are FR-010 through FR-013 consistent about whether the drafted plan remains authoritative once per-phase proposals begin? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK035 Do FR-012's cross-phase check and FR-010's per-phase proposal requirement agree on when the argument is finalized? [Consistency, Spec §FR-010, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK036 Is FR-020's prohibition on distributing implementation work consistent with FR-018's permission to dispatch readers, such that the boundary between the two is stated rather than implied? [Consistency, Spec §FR-018, §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK037 Do FR-025 and FR-026 conflict where the least-discarding choice is also the only one available, leaving no recommendation to make? [Conflict, Spec §FR-025, §FR-026]
- [ ] CHK038 Is the terminology for the two workspace arrangements used consistently — "a branch in the maintainer's own working directory" versus "a separate working directory" — across requirements, scenarios and success criteria? [Consistency, Spec §FR-022, §FR-023, §SC-009]

## Acceptance criteria quality

- [ ] CHK039 Can SC-005's claim of catching leakage "at the same rate as before" be measured, given no baseline rate is recorded? [Measurability, Spec §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK040 Is SC-006's equality between verdict count and boundary count checkable without first defining what counts as a boundary? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK041 Does SC-012 name the check whose passing it requires, or does it depend on a reader knowing which check is meant? [Clarity, Spec §SC-012]
- [ ] CHK042 Are success criteria free of implementation vocabulary, given that the feature's subject matter is itself tooling? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]

## Dependencies and assumptions

- [ ] CHK043 Is the assumption that the conflict-resolution workflow needs no change to be reached validated, or asserted? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK044 Is the assumption that the existing recorded practices are correct as of writing consistent with FR-003's obligation to re-check them? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK045 Are the external documentation sources FR-002 depends on identified, and is the behaviour specified when such a source is unreachable? [Dependency, Gap, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK046 Is the assumption that "the maintainer is the same person who runs the pipeline and reviews its output" load-bearing for any requirement, and if so is that dependency stated? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
- 46 items across 8 categories. Every item carries a traceability reference or a `[Gap]` marker; the three emphases the reviewer named are the first three categories.
